title: Publication, page-scale, and graph runtime closure

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
User-approved Phases 5-7 rationale, preservation boundary, promotion criteria, and explicit deferrals.

allowedWork: Execute only the exact approved 30-slice route, build-time math, CSS ownership, multi-passage lifecycle, physics retained SVG, caller-proven Graph2D, and renderer-neutral Graph3D tranche.

Preserve the current two-column economics route in midnight and paper themes, both text sides, phone behavior, exact semantic frames, accessibility, static export, URL/TOC/Review state, manual control, direct seek, and rewind.
Use IntersectionObserver only for coarse activation, retain one passive rAF-coalesced exact scroll source, keep a bounded live-stage window, and keep Three.js outside 2D route closure.
Keep every slice independently reversible, verified, durably recorded, and committed with exact path staging.
disallowedWork: Do not resume matrix or Lisp animation work, add another tutorial or curriculum domain, build SvelteKit, Internal Studio, Public Web, or either editor.
Do not delete rollback lesson layouts, redesign approved economics or physics visuals, introduce a universal scene graph, or migrate graph callers that do not prove the seam.
Do not make Three.js, runtime KaTeX, code rendering, or WebGL an eager shared dependency, and do not widen performance ceilings to make a check pass.
Do not change semantic truth, domain choreography, accessibility ownership, direct seek, rewind, URL meaning, Review identity, reduced motion, or static/export authority.
goal: Close route and build-time math costs, prove bounded multi-passage behavior, retain the physics SVG runtime, and promote only the graph lifecycle seams proven by economics, physics, and the existing internal Graph3D host.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with exact path staging and completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop on any economics or physics semantic-frame, direct-seek, rewind, accessibility, URL, Review, reduced-motion, static-export, or approved-visual divergence.
Stop if route closure cannot demonstrate measurable dependency reduction without widening current transfer, script, resource, CLS, or long-task ceilings.
Stop on multiple scroll clocks, total-passage-dependent ordinary-scroll geometry reads, visible dehydration layout shift, cross-passage state leakage, or WebGL context exhaustion.
Stop if a shared Graph2D lifecycle requires domain-specific truth or if Graph3D protocol adoption pulls Three.js or WebGL into a 2D route.
Stop on unrelated user-file overlap, missing durable evidence, unsafe authority, or any subjective visual choice outside the approved preservation reference.
Always stop after s30 for explicit human review.
